title: Dendrimer-based Uneven Nanopatterns to Locally Control Surface Adhesiveness: A Method to Direct Chondrogenic Differentiation
protocol: Anneal Au(111) substrate with a butane flame for 3 minutes on a glass-ceramic hob.
Allow annealed Au(111) substrate to cool under an argon atmosphere.
Repeat annealing and cooling steps for each Au(111) substrate immediately after preparation.
Cut microscopy slides into 18 pieces, each measuring 1.25 cm x 1.25 cm using a diamond-tip cutter.
Create a small indentation on the lower side of each cut slide to distinguish upper from lower sides.
Thoroughly wash the slides with deionized water followed by 96% ethanol.
Allow washed slides to air-dry completely.
Add 200 mg of PLLA to 10 mL of 1,4-dioxane in a pressure tube.
Insert a stir bar into the pressure tube and close it tightly.
Place the pressure tube containing the mixture into a glycerin bath on a hot plate at 60 °C with gentle stirring for 24 hours.
Transfer the resulting PLLA solution to a 15-mL glass vial after incubation.
Place coated glass slides and PLLA solution vial on a clean hot plate at 60 °C, ensuring slides are facing upward.
Allow slides to remain on the hot plate for at least 10 minutes to reach necessary temperature.
Place one slide face up on the spin coater using a vacuum system.
Apply 0.25 mL of PLLA solution to the slide with a Pasteur pipette, ensuring full surface coverage.
Run the coating program.
Repeat steps for each slide.
Dissolve 5 mg of dendrimer in 6.494 mL of deionized water to prepare solution A.
Sonicate solution A for 10 minutes.
Prepare solutions B and C following Table 2.
Sonicate solution C for 10 minutes.
Prepare solutions D, E, and F following Table 2.
Store solutions B, C, D, E, and F at 4 °C until use.
Store solution A at -20 °C for later use if necessary.
Sterilize substrates by irradiating with UV light for 13 minutes in a tissue culture hood.
Handle each substrate face up in the wells of a plate carefully using tweezers.
Sonicate solutions B, C, D, E, and F for 10 minutes.
Pass RGD-Cys-D1 dendrimer solutions through a 0.22-µm diameter filter using a syringe directly into the wells containing the substrates (2 mL/well).
Close and seal the plate.
Leave the plate at room temperature for 16 hours.
Remove and discard the solutions.
Wash the substrates with sterile deionized water.
Dry the substrates.
Store the substrates at 4°C.
Sterilize control substrates by irradiating them with UV light for 13 minutes in a tissue culture hood.
Use flame-annealed Au(111) substrates as negative controls.

For positive controls, immerse flame-annealed Au(111) substrates in a solution of RGD-modified PEG thiol (RGD-PEG-SH) and triethylene glycol mono-11-mercaptoundecyl ether (PEG-SH) at a 1:100 molar ratio in 96% ethanol.
Incubate the substrates in this solution for 16 hours at room temperature.
Wash substrates thoroughly in ethanol.
Dry substrates with argon.
Store substrates at 4°C.
Prepare 5 mL of 0.1 mg/mL fibronectin in PBS.
Incubate PLLA substrate with 1.6 mL fibronectin solution for 1 h at room temperature.
Remove and discard the fibronectin solution.
Wash the substrates with PBS.
Store substrates at 4°C.
Perform AFM imaging of PLLA substrates for roughness analysis.
Select a silicon cantilever with a spring constant k = 40 N/m and resonant frequency ν = 300 kHz.
Mount the selected cantilever onto the AFM equipment.
Mount the sample on the stage of the atomic force microscope.
Perform AFM imaging in tapping mode in air.
Approach the sample with the tip of the microscope until contact.
Select at least four representative areas of 20x20 µm per substrate from three independent substrates for imaging PLLA roughness analysis.
Choose at least three representative images of 5×5 µm per substrate from three independent substrates per condition for imaging dendrimer nanopatterns.
Adjust the set point to keep the force at a minimum while imaging to avoid damaging the dendrimer layer.
Process AFM height images by fitting each scan line to polynomial leveling functions using proprietary software.
Analyze processed AFM height images of PLLA to calculate surface roughness.
Obtain image thresholds of processed AFM height images to select dendrimers on the surface.
Determine particle positions using an image processing software.
Use particle positions to obtain the minimum interparticle distances (dmin).
Plot dmin values in z to the corresponding particle positions to obtain probability contour maps for dmin.
Adjust the color scale of the plot to visualize regions of highest local RGD surface density (dmin < 70 nm).
Quantify the area of regions with the highest local RGD surface density using an image processing software.
Include the areas of dendrimer aggregates in the calculation.
Place the nanopatterned substrate in the sample holder of the STM equipment.
Check the electrical connection between sample and holder with a tester.
Etch a tip of the selected probe material (i.e., Pt 0.8: Ir 0.2) with a diameter that ensures proper fitting on the head of the STM equipment.
Mount the tip in the head of the STM equipment and connect the sample.
Set "current" in the feedback channel.
Adjust the bias voltage and current set point and scan size to obtain a well-resolved image once the tip is engaged.
Process the STM topographical images by fitting each scan line to polynomial leveling functions using the proprietary software of the manufacturer of the STM apparatus.
Measure CA on the nanopatterned substrates by the sessile-drop method.
Fill the microsyringe with deionized water and set parameters in the CA software to produce drops of 1 μL.
Place the sample on the stage for clear visibility on the computer.
Move the syringe with the micromanipulator until it gets close to the surface.
Dispense a drop onto the surface.
Record the image immediately after droplet stabilization.
Remove old medium with a 10 mL pipette every 2 days.
Replace with 10 mL of freshly prepared growth medium.
Culture cells until they reach around 80% confluence.
Remove the medium and add 5 mL of trypsin per flask.
Maintain the trypsin solution in contact with the cells for 5 min at 37 °C.
Add 5 mL of growth medium per flask and collect the cells in a centrifuge tube.
Centrifuge the cells at 470 x g for 5 min.
Remove the supernatant and resuspend the cell pellet in 10 mL of growth medium.
Determine the concentration of cells using a hemocytometer.
Transfer the substrates to well plates not treated for tissue culture (non-adherent).
Seed the cells on the substrates at a density of 4,000 cells/cm2 in growth medium.
Incubate them for 4.5 h at 37 °C and 10% CO2 atmosphere.
Culture human MSCs from early passages (<5) at 37 °C and 4.6% CO2 atmosphere in MSC growth medium.
Trypsinize cells before 80% confluence is reached.
Centrifuge and resuspend them in MSC growth medium.
Determine the concentration of cells using a hemocytometer.
Resuspend them in 10 mL of chondrogenesis-inducing medium.
Transfer substrates from plates to new well plates not treated for tissue culture.
Seed cells on the substrates at a density of 3,000 cells/cm².
Change chondrogenic medium every 3 days.
Remove media and wash cells gently with PBS.
Add a 10% formalin solution for 20 min at room temperature to fix cells.
Remove formalin and wash cells with PBS.
Add a 50 mM solution of ammonium chloride (NH4Cl) in PBS to block free aldehyde groups.
Leave the cells for 20 min at room temperature.
Remove NH4Cl solution and wash cells with PBS.
Store samples in PBS at 4 °C if pausing protocol here.
Remove PBS and add a 0.1% saponin solution in blocking solution (1% albumin in PBS) to permeabilize the cells for 10 min at room temperature.
Wash cells with PBS and transfer samples to new well plates.
Incubate cells with primary antibodies in blocking solution for 1 h at room temperature.
Remove primary antibody solution and wash cells with PBS.
Incubate cells with secondary antibodies in blocking solution for 1 h at room temperature, avoiding light exposure.
Remove secondary antibody solution and wash cells with PBS.
Dry the samples.
Cut coverslips into 1.25 cm x 1.25 cm using a diamond-tip cutter.
Apply 50 μL of microscopy mounting medium onto the samples.
Cover the samples gently with cut coverslips.
Transfer the samples to a convenient recipient.
Cover the recipient with aluminum foil.
Store the samples in PBS at 4 °C in the dark until observation.
Place the sample on the stage for imaging using an epifluorescence microscope equipped with digital camera and objectives.
Image cell nuclei with 10X objective using ultraviolet excitation, longpass emission filter to visualize Hoechst/DAPI stain.
Image cell cytoskeleton and focal adhesions (FAs) with 40X objective matching the corresponding antibody fluorochrome specifications.
Use image processing software to convert images to 8-bit files for FA quantification.
Remove background and convert images to binary by setting a threshold.
Compute at least 30 images per sample considering FAs from 1 µm² for calculation.
Image cell condensates at initial stages of chondrogenic induction with an upright epifluorescence microscope.
Use ultraviolet excitation and longpass emission filter to visualize Hoechst/DAPI stain.
Convert images to 8-bit files using image processing software.
Remove background from the images.
Select a threshold that highlights aggregate contour.
Calculate the area of particles in the condensate images.
Image immunostained samples for FAs, cytoskeleton actin fibers, and cartilage-specific collagen type II alpha 1 (COL2A1) with an upright confocal microscope.
Collect sections at high magnification (40-60X).
Process image stacks using image processing software.
Convert images to 8-bit files.
Remove background from the confocal images.
Make the images binary by setting a threshold.
Quantify FA protein stained areas from basal zone of cell condensates and express them as percentage of area divided by number of cell nuclei in the image.
Measure COL2A1 staining using confocal z-projections.
Quantify sum of projected area (maximum COL2A1 area per sample).
Normalize the area value obtained against the area of corresponding condensate.
